result:
The feature was already present when R19 was folded in: `src/builder.rs` had `Covariance`, `try_build` and a five-argument `try_constant_velocity`, so this is completion, not a rebuild.
Landed there: `try_constant_velocity(dims, dt, q, r)` now takes exactly the four requested inputs with P0 = I; the explicit-initial-covariance form is kept as `try_constant_velocity_with_p0`; DESIGN_NOTES.md updated. New `tests/linear_builder.rs` and `tests/linear_constant_velocity.rs` compare each helper with `try_new` exactly, after construction and after each of 20 predict/update steps, in f32 and f64, and compare errors for bad models.
Easy: the existing expand-and-delegate seam (each Covariance becomes a dense slice, then try_new validates) meant no duplicated rules; check_dims/check_len already turn huge or wrong-sized inputs into errors.
Hard: the requested four-parameter helper forces a default initial covariance, so P0 = I; keeping the explicit form avoids losing that ability. The builder still takes n and m beside F and H because memory is sized only after the dimension check.
Unsure: P0 = I gives position and velocity the same variance, weak when their scales differ; the tournament record docs still show the five-argument helper (historical records left untouched).
Verified: frozen 32, lib 114, new 4 + 4, doctests 11, build --all-targets clean; halving the helper's Q makes both precisions fail.
